description: The name list here decides a CLASSIFICATION over request paths rather than over local variable names, and that distinction is the whole reason it works. An attempt to match credential-shaped local names was measured first and abandoned: across twenty clean repositories every match was a counter of language-model tokens -- token_limit, estimated_tokens, truncated_tokens. A request field called `password` is a password. The email in the second route is caller-supplied and is not a credential, and the CSRF token in the third is a credential the page has to read back anyway. The forwarding routes are the same call with the same credential over two schemes, and the qualifier is the whole rule. The echo and issue routes are the pair that shows why the classification is a credential the CALLER SENT: one returns what it was given, and the other returns what it generated. The audit route is the other log weakness, and the two are why a composition requirement had to move off the channel and onto the judgement: a credential is a disclosure whether it was logged whole or built into a sentence, and forging a log LINE requires it to have been built into one.

expected.note: a credential written somewhere durable outlives the request it belonged to
a credential sent over plain HTTP is readable by anyone on the path
a validation response hands the submitted password back to the caller
the caller's text is built into a log line, so a line break makes another entry
